decisions.rationale: The stem now expressly excludes health-examination records for workers who are or were regularly engaged in manufacturing or handling special-management substances, removing the B4 ambiguity between the general five-year rule in Article 40(1) and the thirty-year special rule in Article 40(2). Choice C is therefore uniquely correct. The 30-year distractor tests the exact exception that caused the prior REWORK, while the other periods remain same-domain record-retention confusions. All five choices are explained, and the proposition is distinct from the existing three-month physician-opinion deadline item.

Current Asbestos Ordinance Article 41 requires the asbestos health-examination record to be kept for forty years from the date on which the worker ceases to be regularly engaged in the relevant work at that workplace. Choice D states both the correct starting event and period. The alternatives separately test examination-date, retirement-date and 30-year special-chemical confusions. This is materially distinct from the rejected B4 asbestos six-month examination-frequency item and from the accepted ionizing-radiation frequency item.
